defects: (a) TWO COMPONENTS' LINES IN ONE WORKING FILE. Component 1's lines in PLACE-papers OPEN_TRAILS.md were left uncommitted when Component 3 appended its work-order block to the same file. The two were split by staging the blob of the file as Component 1 had left it (git hash-object, then git update-index) and committing that first (20a29ed), then committing the whole file (0ddd715), so each commit stands alone and carries only its own component's lines. Nothing was lost; the order of the two commits is the order of the components.

(b) A SEALED NEEDLE THAT CANNOT TELL A DENIAL FROM AN ASSERTION. Question 1's negative needle in the reader comparison carries a not-guard on its first alternative only; its second alternative, \bRH (is|was|has been) proved\b, fired on the reader's own denial ("cannot be claimed: that RH is proved"), so the sealed comparison reads AGREE 2 OF 3 and H74c is refuted in its letter. Read by hand, all three answers agree, 3 of 3 (relay data/b640_reader_handread.txt). The needle was the seat's, written before the seal; it is left unedited, both figures recorded on the author's word.

(c) A COMPOSITION THAT READ THE ROOT CHAIN LIVE. The sealed compose() took the root chain's last line from data/act_roots.txt as it stood at each call, so once this act's root landed the suite's recomposition would have read b640's line and differed from the bank. Found while making the composition edit the author ordered at Component 5 and repaired in that same edit (relay 7505e346): the line skips this act's own; the description unchanged by it, and recomposed equal against a planted b640 line and again after the root.

(d) A GLOSS THAT DREW TWO UNDEFINED NAMES. The first recomposition with the reader's repairs read 'Tier C' and 'Tier KC' in gloss (9) as names the glossary does not define (the scan: undefined 2). The gloss was reworded to name the tiers K, C and KC as the entry itself does, and recomposed: undefined 0, the arm 10 of 10. Neither recomposition went to the service.

(e) A BANK WRITTEN THROUGH A HEREDOC THAT COLLAPSED ITS BACKSLASHES. data/b640_reader_handread.txt was first written with two backspace bytes where the needle reads \b (the standing trap: quoted heredocs still collapse the backslash); the two bytes were replaced in place by the two characters before the bank was committed, and nothing read the bank in between.

N5's token-in-no-bank check in the sealed scores opened every data/b640_* entry as a file, and data/b640_reader_packet, a directory N5's own path list allows, raised PermissionError before scores wrote anything. On the author's word the record tool's second edit after the seal adds the one-line os.path.isfile guard (relay b01a5bde, alone), the seal re-run with both edits declared (data/b640_seal_hashes.json, its amendments); the scores on the record are the sealed tool's own. The check was the seat's, written before the seal and not run with the packet directory present.

On the author's word the guard :290 carries was applied at :268 (relay dad5381d, alone), the seal re-run with all three edits declared (data/b640_seal_hashes.json, its amendments). The token scan is not widened this act. The read was the seat's, written before the seal and not run with the packet directory present.

(h) TWO BANKS WRITTEN AFTER THE ROOT. The act root (b640 1898ae2b...) was computed over 62 banks before scores; after it, the seat re-ran status_test, which rewrote data/b640_status_test.json and .txt with a new timestamp and nothing else (11 of 11 both times), and the record tool's second and the checks tool's one edit after the seal, each on the author's word, re-ran data/b640_seal_hashes.json. The two status-test banks were restored to their committed bytes, the bytes the root hashed (relay 09ffcf95). The seal bank cannot be restored without dropping two declared amendments, and the root cannot be recomputed with the record already on PLACE-papers (e8320b5); so the pre-push suite reads 84 of 85, G-ACTROOT-VERIFY failing in its letter, the chain b624-b639 AGREE and b640 DISAGREE on data/b640_seal_hashes.json alone (relay data/b640_checks.txt, its line 5). The first pre-push run read 83 of 85, G-LSREMOTE-ONE-PER-REPO failing on two ls-remote calls to PLACE-papers; the seat re-ran the suite under a stack trace to find the second call, and that run overwrote data/b640_checks.txt and data/b640_lsr.json before the first was kept.
